cards.source_title: Dev Interrupted panel: Why software factories fail without humans
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: every piece of work needs a human owner
cards.claim: Every unit of work in an agent workflow should have a named human owner who answers for it.
cards.evidence_detail: Stated in panel agreement with other panelists; no data. Dan Lines separately cited 37% of agentic PRs merged at low-maturity orgs, but that is not Dex's number.
cards.landing: Phase routine: each PR and register id names one human owner in the Plan @ sha body; the owner view lists items without an owner.
cards.inventory_ref: Related only: Aug 2026 section lists the 2026-08-26 LinearB workshop with the same panelists; this 09-01 transcript is not listed.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: you probably have too many bad PRs because a good PR is a joy to review
cards.claim: A too-many-PRs problem is really a bad-PR problem; fix PR quality and review load stops being the pain.
cards.evidence_detail: Opinion with a reviewer-experience argument; no measurement.
cards.landing: Reviewer instruction: reject on rework burden, not volume; reduce bad PRs upstream with the closing six-question message.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: If something needs like less than 5% rework
cards.claim: A PR needing under about 5% rework is the quality bar at which review is painless and re-reviewing a thousand is fine.
cards.evidence_detail: A single threshold quoted as a heuristic, no study behind it.
cards.landing: A measurable per-PR rework-rate target (share of diff changed after reviewer feedback) recorded in the decisions journal.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: created a very tight gate of what can be auto-merged
cards.claim: Three CTOs (30-40 engineers each) set a narrow auto-merge gate (code areas, size, deterministic or small-classifier criteria); PRs that pass checks skip review.
cards.evidence_detail: Second-hand report from three CTOs in San Francisco on teams of about 100+ people; no figures beyond the example of under 200 lines.
cards.landing: CI-side gate on import-boundary contracts, diff size and paths touched, deciding which PRs can skip the Opus reviewer.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: the PR numbers went way up
cards.claim: An auto-merge gate changed engineer behaviour: PR count rose and giant slop PRs stopped, because small PRs avoiding core systems skip the wait for review.
cards.evidence_detail: Reported outcome from the same three CTOs; no numbers. Dex flags the unknown downside of harmful changes slipping past the rules.
cards.landing: Incentive design: make the cheap path (small, outside core) the one with lighter review, so agents and authors self-shape diffs.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: measure the amount of tokens shipped
cards.claim: Measurement ladder: customer outcomes first, then features shipped, PRs, lines of code, and tokens only as the last-resort proxy.
cards.evidence_detail: Ranking given verbally with the GitLab practice of handing developers customer problems, not tickets.
cards.landing: Harness metrics: prefer outcome-ish measures (fail-before/pass-after per register id) over tokens or PR counts; treat token spend as a cost line only.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: each optimize, like, one particular station in the factory
cards.claim: Optimising one stage (e.g. review) without looking at end-to-end throughput repeats the factory-optimisation mistake in The Goal.
cards.evidence_detail: Analogy to the 1970s book The Goal; no data.
cards.landing: Judge a verifier or review step by whole-phase throughput and escaped defects, not by its own pass rate.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: every change that comes out of the factory is compounded into
cards.claim: Unlike physical goods, each shipped change affects all later changes, so past slop taxes every future task until fixed.
cards.evidence_detail: Conceptual argument; no numbers.
cards.landing: Count debt left behind by a phase (the decisions journal) as a cost of that phase, with follow-up items owned.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: you basically have two zones of your code base
cards.claim: Split the codebase into a high-standard core and a slop-tolerated pragmatic zone; zones may not import from each other, and shared code must be promoted into the core.
cards.evidence_detail: Attributed to Ben Swerdlow's team and to principal engineers at larger teams; no numbers.
cards.landing: Extend the existing import-linter contracts with zone tiers and tie review depth to zone; CLAUDE.md slice-boundary rule already points this way.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: agents are probably the most unreliable
cards.claim: Front end (React, many useEffects) is a place agents are least reliable, contra the view that it is a safe zone for slop; Factory AI banned useEffect for this reason.
cards.evidence_detail: From many customers plus a third-party post (Factory AI); no data. Disagrees with Aloke Desai's view.
cards.landing: Web manager (React 19) work gets stricter review than assumed; consider lint rules limiting useEffect.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: We ran a lights off Factory for, like, four or five months
cards.claim: His team ran a lights-off factory for 4-5 months on Opus 4.1 with best-in-class prompting and harness, ended with a tangled front end, and rebuilt from scratch on good patterns as faster than evolving it.
cards.evidence_detail: First-hand experience, duration given, no quality measurements.
cards.landing: Evidence against hands-off autonomy for FixFlow phases; supports human checkpoints above the diff.
cards.inventory_ref: Section B July 2026: Pragmatic Engineer podcast and wsff.md cover the lights-off failure, not this panel.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: I published a skill like two weeks ago called /showme
cards.claim: A skill that distills a diff into readable snippets, diffs and diagrams raises understanding bandwidth; understanding cannot be outsourced.
cards.evidence_detail: Product description, no measurement.
cards.landing: Add show-me (humanlayer/skills) or a similar summary skill under .claude/skills/ for the owner view and reviewer.
cards.inventory_ref: A3 table (2026-08-12 show-me post) and Aug 2026 section

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: you cannot outsource the thinking
cards.claim: If you lose touch with what is happening in the codebase, faster understanding tools are the remedy; the thinking and understanding stay with humans.
cards.evidence_detail: Stated as principle.
cards.landing: Closing message and owner view should be built for fast human comprehension (visual, short), not full diff dumps.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: save you three hours of PR review time by spending 20 minutes reviewing a spec
cards.claim: Shift human review upstream: 20 minutes on a spec with a coworker can save about three hours of PR review.
cards.evidence_detail: Illustrative figures stated in a product pitch; no study.
cards.landing: Human gate on the plan (Plan @ sha) before implementation, rather than only at the diff.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Don't complain or throw stuff over the wall
cards.claim: Engineers should fix the shared pipeline (e.g. slow CI) themselves; maintaining and improving the factory is everyone's job.
cards.evidence_detail: Cultural principle.
cards.landing: Treat repeated agent failures as harness bugs and save the fix as a skill or workflow script.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: we haven't figured out how to RL into AI
cards.claim: Lessons humans learn from past pain (3am debugging) are not in model weights, so humans must keep applying that intuition to review.
cards.evidence_detail: Opinion on current training limits.
cards.landing: Capture hard-won incident lessons as explicit rules in CLAUDE.md or a store, as FixFlow already does under 'Each of these was paid for'.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: unified observability across SDLC is missing
cards.claim: Plans, session traces, specs, designs and code live in disconnected tools (copy-pasting agent output through Slack is like emailing git patches); a native tool linking them is the opportunity.
cards.evidence_detail: Reads a chat comment aloud and then adds his own diagram-based vision; no data. Product vision for HumanLayer.
cards.landing: Keep plan, journal and evidence in-repo and linked from the PR so a cold-resume agent finds them; session traces are the missing link behind W2.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: a little bit lower bar for the code quality
cards.claim: The pragmatic zone gets a lower review bar than core code, so review effort is allocated by zone.
cards.evidence_detail: Policy described from other teams; no numbers.
cards.landing: Route verifier effort by zone: heavy refuters on money, auth, outbox invariants; lighter elsewhere (ties to effort routing).

cards.source_title: What We Heard at AGNTCon Europe (JetBrains Blog)
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: code from unattended agents gets worse over time
cards.claim: In his State of the Software Factory keynote he argued unattended agent code degrades over time, so for now people must plan before building and keep reading the code.
cards.evidence_detail: Third-party paraphrase (Katherine Druckman) of a keynote; no data quoted. Wording is the recap writer's, not his.
cards.landing: Supports human plan and code-reading gates in the phase routine; supports one-phase-per-session with owner review.
cards.inventory_ref: Related: Sept 2026 section lists the WeAreDevelopers State of the Software Factory talk (2026-09-23/25); this Amsterdam keynote (2026-09-17) and the JetBrains recap are not listed.

cards.source_title: What We Heard at AGNTCon Europe (JetBrains Blog)
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: added agentic code review and regression testing to the production pipeline
cards.claim: His keynote diagram adds agentic code review and regression testing to the pipeline, and notes review can still be the bottleneck.
cards.evidence_detail: Recap of a slide; no figures.
cards.landing: Confirms review and regression gates as pipeline stages; review throughput is a constraint to plan for, not eliminate.

cards.source_title: What We Heard at AGNTCon Europe (JetBrains Blog)
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Lights-Off Software Factory
cards.claim: He presented a diagram of a lights-off factory (no human review) as the setup he argues against.
cards.evidence_detail: Caption on a photo of his slide; no content beyond the label.
cards.landing: Negative design reference: do not run FixFlow phases without a human review step.

cards.source_title: code.talks 2026 Hamburg: Why Software Factories Fail (abstract)
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: trained to make the test pass, not to improve the codebase
cards.claim: Models are trained to make tests pass, not to improve the codebase over time, so output is locally correct but globally corrosive; no prompt or code fixes this.
cards.evidence_detail: Abstract only; same thesis as wsff.md in inventory; no data in this page.
cards.landing: Do not treat green tests as sufficient acceptance; verifiers must check structure (import contracts, blast radius) as well as pass/fail.
cards.inventory_ref: Section B July 2026 (wsff.md, 'Why Software Factories Fail' essay 2026-07-22/23); the code.talks page itself is not listed

cards.source_title: code.talks 2026 Hamburg: Why Software Factories Fail (abstract)
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: maintainability, navigability, blast radius, outcomes over time
cards.claim: A better benchmark would measure maintainability, navigability, blast radius and outcomes over time.
cards.evidence_detail: Listed in an abstract as what a better benchmark must measure; no method given.
cards.landing: Candidate verifier axes for FixFlow reviewers: blast radius per diff, navigability for a cold-resume agent, outcomes tracked after merge.

cards.source_title: code.talks 2026 Hamburg: Why Software Factories Fail (abstract)
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: They can write code; they can't yet do architecture.
cards.claim: Until models can architect, judgment must re-enter the loop above the code: humans decide what gets built, a level up from the diff, as the steering wheel.
cards.evidence_detail: Abstract thesis; no data.
cards.landing: Human decisions belong at the plan and architecture level (Plan @ sha) rather than line review; guides what the owner view shows.

cards.source_title: code.talks 2026 Hamburg: Why Software Factories Fail (abstract)
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: many teams learned the hard way that agents can't be trusted
cards.claim: After a hype cycle (Ralph, strongDM) the spring cool-off showed agents can't be trusted in a production codebase without human judgment.
cards.evidence_detail: Narrative history in an abstract; no numbers.
cards.landing: Background for keeping the refute-by-default and human-owner stance; pairs with the unattended-loop caution.

gaps: The JetBrains recap covers Dex's Amsterdam keynote (State of the Software Factory, 2026-09-17) in a single paragraph; no keynote content beyond that is available from this bundle.
The code.talks page is only an abstract and bio; no talk content, slides or numbers.
In the panel, the auto-merge gate is described with only one concrete threshold (under about 200 lines); no stated rework, defect or throughput numbers for gated PRs.
The panel contains no mention of CLAUDE.md length, hooks, effort levels, context windows or compaction; W1, W4 (aside from the skill mention) and L1/L2 get no direct evidence from this bundle.
Dex's /showme skill is called a skill published about two weeks before 2026-09-01; the panel gives no repo link or install detail.
